headline: Gradient’s assumptions imply more equity lowers risk-adjusted return in every scenario
takeaway: Why: Gradient assumes bonds earn more per unit of risk on their own (0.37) than developed or emerging equity (0.36 and 0.35) and are nearly uncorrelated with them (−0.03), so each step from bonds into equities lowers the ratio. On these assumptions it would peak near 26% equity (0.54), which shows how much the result rests on the bond assumptions; return targets, not this ratio alone, set equity weights.
